Synopsis:
    Manpreet Kohli, CEO of crypto project Saitama, lost his extradition fight in a UK court on Aug 19. He faces transfer to the US on wire fraud and market manipulation charges, accused of a pump-and-dump scheme on a token that once reached $7.5B market cap. A Boston federal court also rejected his bid to dismiss the US indictment. Ministerial sign-off on extradition is pending; Kohli remains on bail and retains appeal rights.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US stock market pricing?
Relevance: IMPLICIT — The case touches on US regulatory reach over crypto markets and the ongoing legal framework around digital asset classification as securities, which has broader implications for crypto market structure and sentiment, but no direct link to macro pricing or rates.

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: 15 — The FBI crypto sting operation and Saitama fraud case have been publicly known since 2024. This article reports a procedural legal update (extradition ruling), not a new or unexpected risk. The outcome is largely consistent with typical extradition proceedings.
